newsitem.title: UK: Fitch gives AIG-Hyperion PIBOR A/V2 fund rating.
newsitem.headline: Fitch gives AIG-Hyperion PIBOR A/V2 fund rating.

text.p: Fitch Investors Service said on Monday it had assigned AIG-Hyperion PIBOR ABS Fund Plc, an open-ended Dublin registered investment company with variable capital, a bond fund rating of A/V-2.
"This rating marks the first time Fitch has applied its bond fund ratings to a non-U.S. domiciled fund," Fitch said in a statement.
"Bond funds are assigned credit ratings commensurate with the overall credit quality of investments in the fund's portfolio," said Fitch.

"Funds rated A are considered to have high credit quality. The weighted average default probability of the fund's portfolio securities is consistent with that of the default probability associated with an A rated debt obligation," the agency said.

Fitch said additionally, bond funds are assigned volatility ratings to describe the relative sensitivity of the fund's total return and net asset value (NAV) to changes in interest rates, currency exchange rates and other general market conditions.

Volatility ratings are assigned on a scale of V1 plus (least volatile) through V10 (most volatile). The V1 plus rating is assigned exclusively to money market mutual funds and other funds whose intent is to maintain a stable principal value while V1 through V10 is reserved for fluctuating NAV funds, said Fitch.

It said bond funds rated V2 are considered to have low market risk. Total returns are expected to exhibit relative stability, performing consistently across a broad range of interest rate and currency exchange rate scenarios.

"The AIG-Hyperion PIBOR ABS Fund affords non-U.S. citizens the opportunity to earn incremental yield by taking advantage of the higher yielding U.S. and European mortgage-backed and asset-backed markets," said Fitch.

"Specifically, the objective of the fund is to generate a French Franc denominated return in excess of the three month Paris Interbank Offered Rate (PIBOR) while maintaining a relatively stable NAV per share."
"Income will be accumulated by the fund and reflected in the price of the shares. The purchase of shares is precluded for either Irish residents or U.S. persons," Fitch said.
AIG Asset Manager Limited, as manager of the fund, had appointed AIG-Hyperion Investment Management L.P (AIG-HIM) to act as the investment manager, said Fitch.

"As such, AIG-HIM is responsible for investment decisions and the implementation of the hedging strategy. AIG-HIM, registered in the U.S. as an investment advisor, is a joint venture between AIG Investment Corporation and Hyperion Capital Management (Hyperion)," said Fitch.

"The fund was incorporated in Ireland on May 7th, 1996 and is listed on the Irish Stock Exchange. Chase Funds Management Services (Ireland) Limited and Chase Manhattan Bank (Ireland) plc, both wholly-owned subsidiaries of The Chase Manhattan Corporation, serve as administrator to the fund and custodian of the fund's assets, respectively," Fitch said.
